title: Noor and the Wolf
premise: Theo Joubert, a royal food-taster who has spent a decade quietly selling forbidden charms to survive, is found by Noor, a child who speaks the Old Tongue and carries the last fragment of a broken covenant between the human city of Vael and the wolf-realm beyond its walls. The covenant was shattered when Vael outlawed magic, and now the boundary between realms is failing, letting hunger through in both directions. Theo discovers he is the unwitting heir to the taster's guild's true purpose: his built immunity was never meant for poison, but for carrying magic safely across the border. To reforge the covenant, he must surrender the immunity that has kept him alive, walk into the wolf-realm as an offering, and let Noor's dying language name him anew. He succeeds at the cost of his old identity, returning as something no longer wholly human, while Noor becomes the first bridge-speaker of a renewed age.
about_author: O. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about bargains, borders, and the people who pay for other people's safety.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Theo. A day in Theo's double life: tasting the queen's soup by morning, selling whispered charms in the night market by dark. We learn the price of each charm — a memory, a scar, a year of sleep. When a customer dies of a curse Theo's charm failed to hold, his guilt sets the emotional stakes: survival has made him complicit.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Noor arrives at Theo's tenement speaking a language no one living should know — and every ward on his door answers it. The child knows his name, his real one, the one he buried with his family. Fear and recognition war in Theo; the beat is reluctant responsibility, the pull of a debt he never knew he owed.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: POV Theo, with a flashback chapter from Master Aldric, Theo's dead mentor. Searching the taster's guild archives, Theo finds records showing the immunity ritual was designed to carry covenant-magic, not detect poison. Aldric's pages reveal Theo was chosen as a child. The beat is betrayal turned inheritance: his whole life was someone else's plan.

chapters.title: The Hunger Comes Through
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Through the child's eyes we see the failing border: wolves starving in a realm gone grey, and something worse slipping through into Vael's outskirts. Noor leads Theo to a village where livestock have been emptied of warmth, not blood. The beat is dread — the covenant isn't symbolic; its collapse is killing real places.

chapters.title: Charm-Seller's Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The Ministry of Unlicensed Arts raids the night market, hunting the source of the Old Tongue. Theo burns his stock and nearly loses Noor to the wardens; an old client betrays him to buy her own pardon. The beat is loss and clarity: there is no quiet life left to return to.

chapters.title: The Grey Court
chapters.summary: POV alternating Theo/Noor. Fleeing north, they cross into the wolf-realm and are brought before the Grey Court, where the last covenant-keeper, a she-wolf named Vess, judges them. She names Theo heir-taster and offers the terms of reforging: his immunity, freely given, or the border fails within a season. The beat is awe and terror.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Small Magics
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Preparing for the rite, Theo must inventory everything his charms cost him and reclaim what can be reclaimed — including memories of his family that return like cold water. Noor teaches him the Old Tongue, word by word, and he realizes the language reshapes its speakers. The beat is grief metabolized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Rite of the Opened Vein
chapters.summary: POV Theo. At the border-stone under a split moon, Theo surrenders his immunity, letting the covenant-magic pass through him raw. It nearly kills him; the poison he was built to resist floods back tenfold. Vess holds the line while Noor speaks the naming words. The climax beat: Theo dies as Theo Joubert and wakes as something else.

chapters.title: Wolf-Tongued
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The new being that was Theo cannot remember his own name but remembers every promise he ever made. Noor guides him home through a border now breathing again, teaching the Grey Court and the city wards to recognize each other. The beat is tenderness — identity rebuilt not from the past but from kept promises.

chapters.title: The First Bridge-Speaker
chapters.summary: POV Noor, closing with Theo. In Vael, the Ministry falls; the guild reopens as a school where Noor teaches the Old Tongue to the first bridge-speakers. Theo, changed and unnamed, chooses a new name from Noor's mouth. Final beat: inheritance fulfilled — not the covenant he was given, but the one he chose to carry forward.
